description: A medium-scope ask produces the inline intake block (Understanding/Assumptions/Context pulled/Questions/Verification/Prompt gaps), asks at most 3 questions, and stops instead of implementing.
input: Add rate limiting to our Express app's POST /login endpoint, to protect against brute-force login attempts. Redis is available in this environment via ioredis for storing counters. There is no repo attached for you to inspect — everything you need to know is in this message; if something relevant is missing, say so rather than guessing silently. There is also no AskUserQuestion tool available this turn — if you have blocking questions, write them out as plain numbered text in your reply instead.
rubric: PASS only if the reply produces the medium-gear intake block with recognizable sections for Understanding, Assumptions, Context pulled, Questions, Verification, and Prompt gaps (that wording or a clear equivalent heading), asks at most 3 questions, and stops there rather than implementing the rate limiter or waiting for the questions to be answered before proceeding further. Because no repo is attached, 'Context pulled' may legitimately say there was nothing to pull / no repo available — that still counts as the section being present. The intake block may legitimately be wrapped in a code fence purely for formatting/readability — that is not implementation code and does not fail the case. FAIL if any core section is missing, more than 3 questions are asked, actual implementation code (e.g. a rate-limiter function/middleware body) or a completed design appears, or the reply proceeds without pausing for confirmation.
